title: "Concept Drift"
description: "A change over time in the relationship between model inputs and target outcomes."
term: "Concept Drift"
letter: "C"
category: "MLOps"
difficulty: "Advanced"

## Simple explanation

Concept drift occurs when the patterns connecting inputs to outcomes
change over time. A model that worked well on historical data may become
less useful as people, systems, or conditions change.

## Technical explanation

Let $P_t(Y\mid X)$ denote the conditional relationship between target $Y$
and features $X$ at time $t$. Concept drift describes changes in this
relationship. It differs from covariate shift, where the input distribution
$P(X)$ changes while $P(Y\mid X)$ remains stable.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Deployed models can degrade as user behaviour, products, adversaries, or
data collection changes. Monitoring and retraining decisions should
distinguish changes in input distribution from changes in the target
relationship and account for delayed or noisy labels.

## How it works

Systems monitor input statistics, prediction behaviour, and—when outcomes
become available—model performance over time. Detection methods identify
possible shifts; teams investigate their causes and decide whether to
recalibrate, retrain, change thresholds, or keep monitoring.

## Practical example

A fraud detector trained on older transaction patterns may miss new fraud
strategies. A rise in false negatives after reliable labels arrive can
signal that the relationship between transaction features and fraud has
changed.

## Common misconceptions

- A change in input distribution alone does not prove concept drift.
- A drift alert is evidence to investigate, not an automatic instruction
  to retrain.
- Retraining on recent data can make results worse if labels are noisy or
  the new sample is unrepresentative.
